charts/server.json, written by servtuner analyze for the Server and Resources tabs: the server-side series the analysis reads, as the analysis derives them (pods selected, units normalized), and each target container's CPU and memory on its busiest pod with the captured requests and limits as reference lines. Each series has at most 2000 points that keep each bucket's minimum and maximum. A series that was not collected is absent: no evidence, never zero.

Schema file: `schema/json/bundle/chart-server.schema.json`. Generated from servtuner commit `5730cfa50f08`.

## Top level

| Field              | Type                                                                 | Required | Description                                                                |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `analyzer_version` | `string`                                                             | Yes      |                                                                            |
| `start`            | [utcTimestamp](/reference/schemas/common/#utctimestamp)              | Yes      | The first stage's start; every offset is from here.                        |
| `bucket_seconds`   | `integer`                                                            | Yes      | Seconds per point, chosen to keep at most 2000 points over the stages. ≥ 1 |
| `panels`           | array of [serverPanel](/reference/schemas/chart-server/#serverpanel) | Yes      |                                                                            |

## Definitions

### panelGroup

server: the target application's own series (queues, caches, router slots, GPU); resources: CPU and memory against requests and limits.

Type: `"server"`, `"resources"`

### panelUnit

fraction is 0 to 1 (of a limit, a knob or a capacity). per\_second is events per second (the panel title names the event); tokens\_per\_second is tokens per second; seconds is a duration; watts is power; hertz is a clock frequency.

Type: `"fraction"`, `"requests"`, `"pods"`, `"cores"`, `"bytes"`, `"seconds"`, `"per_second"`, `"tokens_per_second"`, `"watts"`, `"hertz"`
